title: AMD-specific fork of llama.cpp
lede: A blog post recommends llama-cpp-rdna-boosts, a small set of AMD patches for llama.cpp that the author says lifted generation from 35 to 55 tokens per second.

points: The patches apply to a pinned llama.cpp commit and are re-applied as upstream moves, keeping the fork small.
On an R9700 over eGPU running a 27B Qwen 3.8 model, prefill went from 700 to 1300 tokens per second.
The author warns that some new bespoke engines, such as Strata, gain speed by changing which experts the model uses.
Prebuilt ROCm server images run under podman, so there is no need to build against local ROCm libraries.

points.text: Several commenters report doubling or tripling speed with their own Claude-assisted forks, on an MI100 and on 7900XTX cards.
Owners of 2018-era gfx906 cards with fast HBM2 memory note that patches aimed at newer RDNA cards do nothing for them.
Asked why llama.cpp does not merge these changes, a reply suggests they would cause regressions on other supported architectures.
Intel Arc owners ask for similar patches, saying the XMX units go largely unused on Linux.
